summary: test/smoke_container.sh (the router image smoke test, CI job container and local runs) now checks its shell after option parsing and before any engine call: when uname -s reports a Windows POSIX layer (*_NT-*, MINGW*, MSYS*, CYGWIN*; Git Bash, MSYS2 incl. UCRT64/CLANG64, Cygwin) it prints the state, the reason (these shells rewrite the container paths the script passes, so only the build worked and --check, --init and the self-tests failed with 'invalid option type') and a wsl command for this checkout, then exits 2 with STATE: refused. --help and unknown options behave as before; on Linux the check is a no-op and the script continues to the unchanged engine, curl and Dockerfile checks, so CI's container job (ubuntu-latest, --engine docker) is unaffected. The script gains no new input: uname output, the checkout path and the caller's own options only flow into the printed message, never into a command the script runs. Traced: option parsing, refuse(), cleanup trap (not yet installed at the check, so nothing to clean), the CI invocations in .github/workflows/ci.yml (unchanged). test/selftest_container_image.py (CI python job, Linux) runs the script with stand-in uname, docker and podman on PATH: refusal for four Windows system names without any engine call, the Linux case reaching the engine check, and the suggested command repeating only inert text. Docs: CHANGELOG tooling section, design/router-container.md and the AGENTS.md check list name the Linux/WSL requirement. No router or agent code, configuration key, endpoint, dependency, workflow or trust boundary changes; TM-16 is named because the script runs in CI, whose steps and pins are unchanged.

findings.evidence: In the first draft of this change the suggested command embedded the checkout path and the caller's options via printf %q inside a single-quoted bash -c string. %q falls back to $'...' quoting for control characters, which ends the surrounding single quotes, so a checkout folder named with a newline and $(...) would have run a command in the user's shell when the printed hint was pasted. Never committed.
findings.resolution: The hint now repeats only shell-inert text (inert(): letters, digits and / . _ + : @ = -, the path additionally spaces inside double quotes); anything else becomes a placeholder (<value>, /mnt/c/<checkout>). Rejected-case test test_suggested_command_repeats_only_inert_text passes an option with $(...), a quote, ; and backticks and asserts the placeholder and that none of them is echoed; checked by hand in Git Bash with a checkout folder named 'odd $(touch pwned) dir' (placeholder printed, no file created) and one with a space (quoted path).

tests.evidence: 20 tests OK (17 before plus 3 in SmokeScriptTests). Against origin/main's smoke_container.sh the new class fails 5 times (4 Windows system names, inert-text case); the Linux case passes on both, so Linux behaviour is unchanged.

The build/start path is unchanged by this change; CI's container job runs it on Linux with Docker.

limitations: shellcheck is not installed locally; the script was checked with bash -n, the self-test on Linux and manual runs in Git Bash.

Cygwin and MSYS2's own shells were not run; their uname -s names (CYGWIN_NT-*, MSYS_NT-*, UCRT64_NT-*) are covered by the stand-in test only. The drive-path derivation (/c/... and /cygdrive/c/... to /mnt/c/...) ran in real Git Bash for /d/... only.
The hint suggests the Podman machine as an example; with Docker Desktop the user picks their own WSL distribution.
